about: Reclaim knowledge base. Patterns: '?:' = any drive, '*' = one path segment, '**' = any number of segments, '%USERS%' = '?:\Users\*'. kind 'dir' matches folders, 'file' matches files. Most specific pattern (most literal characters) wins. Unmatched space is UNKNOWN and is never auto-approved. Machine-specific entries go in kb/local.json (same format, not published).

entries.name: Hibernation file
entries.creator: Windows power management (kernel)
entries.purpose: Holds a copy of RAM so the PC can hibernate, and lets Fast Startup resume the kernel session at boot.
entries.breaks: Hibernate and Fast Startup stop working. Cold boots may take a few seconds longer.
entries.regenerates: yes - recreated when hibernation is turned back on
entries.method: Turn hibernation off from an elevated prompt; Windows removes the file itself. To keep Fast Startup with a smaller file, use the reduced type instead.
entries.command: powercfg /hibernate off      (keep Fast Startup, smaller file: powercfg /hibernate /type reduced)

entries.name: Paging file (virtual memory)
entries.creator: Windows memory manager
entries.purpose: Backs RAM when memory runs short and receives the kernel crash dump after a blue screen.
entries.breaks: Programs can crash with out-of-memory errors and blue screens leave no dump. Move it to another fixed drive rather than removing it.
entries.regenerates: yes - recreated at boot while a paging file is configured for the drive
entries.method: System Properties > Advanced > Performance Settings > Advanced > Virtual memory > Change: set C: to 'No paging file', give another fixed drive 'System managed size', reboot.
entries.command: SystemPropertiesPerformance.exe      (then Advanced > Virtual memory > Change; elevated)

entries.name: Store-app swap file
entries.creator: Windows memory manager
entries.purpose: Swaps suspended Microsoft Store (UWP) apps out of RAM.
entries.breaks: Store apps resume more slowly. It is removed only together with the drive's paging file.
entries.method: Follows pagefile.sys: it goes away only when the drive's paging file is disabled.

entries.name: Previous Windows installation
entries.creator: Windows Setup (feature update or in-place upgrade)
entries.purpose: Lets you roll back to the previous Windows version; Windows normally removes it after 10 days.
entries.breaks: You can no longer go back to the previous Windows version. Files left in the old installation (including old user profiles) become unrecoverable once it is cleaned.
entries.regenerates: only on the next feature upgrade
entries.method: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > 'Previous Windows installation(s)', or Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files.
entries.command: cleanmgr.exe /d C:      (elevated; Clean up system files > Previous Windows installation(s))

entries.name: WinRE update staging ($WinREAgent)
entries.creator: Windows Update (Windows Recovery Environment servicing)
entries.purpose: Staging area for Windows Recovery Environment updates; normally removed when the update finishes.
entries.breaks: Nothing once no WinRE update is pending; an in-progress WinRE update would fail and retry.
entries.method: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files.
entries.command: cleanmgr.exe /d C:      (elevated; Clean up system files)

entries.name: Windows upgrade temporary files
entries.creator: Windows Setup / Update Assistant / Media Creation Tool
entries.purpose: Temporary files from a Windows upgrade or from downloading install media.
entries.breaks: An upgrade that is staged right now would have to download again.
entries.regenerates: yes - on the next upgrade attempt
entries.method: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > 'Temporary Windows installation files'.
entries.command: cleanmgr.exe /d C:      (elevated; Clean up system files > Temporary Windows installation files)

entries.name: Windows Update download cache
entries.creator: Windows Update service (wuauserv)
entries.purpose: Holds downloaded update packages until they are installed.
entries.breaks: Pending updates download again. Nothing else.
entries.method: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > 'Windows Update Cleanup' (service-aware).
entries.command: cleanmgr.exe /d C:      (elevated; Clean up system files > Windows Update Cleanup)

entries.name: Windows Update database
entries.creator: Windows Update service (wuauserv)
entries.purpose: Update history database (DataStore) and service state.
entries.breaks: Update history is lost and Windows Update does a full rescan. Do not move by hand.
entries.regenerates: partly - rebuilt by a full update rescan
entries.method: Leave it. The download subfolder is handled separately.

entries.name: Windows temp folder
entries.creator: Windows services, drivers and installers running as SYSTEM
entries.purpose: Scratch space for system-level processes and installers.
entries.breaks: Files in use are locked and stay put. An installer running right now could fail.
entries.method: Quarantine from an elevated run (locked files are left in place), or Settings > Storage > Temporary files.

entries.name: User temp folder
entries.creator: Programs and installers run by that user
entries.purpose: Scratch files; most are left behind by programs that never clean up after themselves.
entries.breaks: Files in use are locked and stay put. Programs open right now may lose their scratch data.
entries.method: Close open programs, then quarantine. Locked files are skipped and reported.

entries.name: Windows Installer cache
entries.creator: Windows Installer (msiexec)
entries.purpose: Cached .msi/.msp packages needed to repair, patch and uninstall installed programs.
entries.breaks: Uninstall, repair and patching of MSI-installed programs fail (Office, Visual Studio, drivers, runtimes).
entries.method: Never remove by hand. Uninstall programs you no longer need; their cached packages go with them.

entries.name: Component store (WinSxS)
entries.creator: Windows servicing (CBS / TrustedInstaller)
entries.purpose: Every system component version. Most files are hard links shared with System32, so the size shown here is overcounted.
entries.breaks: Windows can become unbootable or unrepairable. Never touch by hand.
entries.method: Measure the real size and superseded components with DISM, and clean only with DISM.
entries.command: Dism.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /AnalyzeComponentStore      (then only if recommended: Dism.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup; both elevated)
entries.notes: Hard links are counted once per link, so this total is larger than the real usage.

entries.name: Kernel minidumps
entries.creator: Windows crash dump (written after a blue screen)
entries.purpose: Small crash dumps for diagnosing blue screens.
entries.breaks: Evidence of past crashes is gone from this location.
entries.method: Quarantine from an elevated run.

entries.name: Full kernel memory dump
entries.creator: Windows crash dump (written after a blue screen)
entries.purpose: Complete kernel memory dump from the last blue screen.
entries.breaks: Evidence of the last crash is gone from this location.
entries.method: Quarantine from an elevated run.

entries.name: Live kernel reports
entries.creator: Windows kernel watchdog
entries.purpose: Dumps written when a driver hangs without a full crash (often GPU timeouts).
entries.breaks: Diagnostic dumps are gone from this location.
entries.regenerates: yes - after the next driver hang
entries.method: Quarantine from an elevated run.

entries.name: Event logs
entries.creator: Windows Event Log service
entries.purpose: System, Application, Security and per-component event logs.
entries.breaks: Log history is lost. The files are locked by the service and cannot be moved.
entries.regenerates: yes - logs grow up to their configured maximum size
entries.method: Find the largest logs: Get-WinEvent -ListLog * | Sort-Object FileSize -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 LogName,FileSize,MaximumSizeInBytes. Lower a log's maximum size in Event Viewer, or clear one log.
entries.command: wevtutil cl <LogName>      (elevated; erases that log's history - Reclaim never runs this)

entries.name: Servicing logs (CBS / DISM)
entries.creator: Windows servicing (TrustedInstaller) and DISM
entries.purpose: Logs of update installs and repairs. CBS.log can grow to gigabytes when servicing loops.
entries.breaks: History for troubleshooting failed updates is gone. The current log is locked and stays.
entries.method: Quarantine from an elevated run.

entries.name: Windows Error Reporting (all users)
entries.creator: Windows Error Reporting
entries.purpose: Queued and archived crash reports.
entries.breaks: Crash reports not yet sent to Microsoft are gone.
entries.method: Quarantine from an elevated run.

entries.name: Windows Error Reporting (this user)
entries.creator: Windows Error Reporting
entries.purpose: Queued and archived crash reports for this user's programs.
entries.breaks: Crash reports not yet sent to Microsoft are gone.
entries.method: Quarantine.

entries.name: Application crash dumps
entries.creator: Windows Error Reporting (LocalDumps) when a program crashes
entries.purpose: Memory dumps of crashed programs.
entries.breaks: Dumps for diagnosing app crashes are gone.
entries.regenerates: yes - after the next app crash
entries.method: Quarantine.

entries.name: Chrome caches
entries.creator: Google Chrome
entries.purpose: Downloaded page resources, compiled scripts, GPU shaders and web-app offline caches.
entries.breaks: Sites load slower the first time; offline copies kept by web apps are dropped. Logins and cookies are stored elsewhere and stay.
entries.method: Close Chrome, then quarantine. Alternative: chrome://settings/clearBrowserData > Cached images and files.

entries.name: Edge caches
entries.creator: Microsoft Edge
entries.purpose: Downloaded page resources, compiled scripts, GPU shaders and web-app offline caches.
entries.breaks: Sites load slower the first time; offline copies kept by web apps are dropped. Logins and cookies stay.
entries.method: Close Edge (including background: Settings > System > 'Continue running background extensions' off), then quarantine.

entries.name: npm cache
entries.creator: npm (Node.js package manager)
entries.purpose: Content-addressed cache of every package tarball npm has downloaded.
entries.breaks: Next installs download packages again; offline installs fail until then.
entries.regenerates: yes - on the next npm install
entries.method: Quarantine, or let npm clear it.

entries.name: pip cache
entries.creator: pip (Python package installer)
entries.purpose: Downloaded wheels and HTTP cache.
entries.breaks: Next installs download again.
entries.regenerates: yes - on the next pip install
entries.method: Quarantine, or let pip clear it.

entries.name: pnpm store
entries.creator: pnpm (Node.js package manager)
entries.purpose: Global content-addressed store; every project's node_modules hard-links into it.
entries.breaks: Projects keep working (hard links keep the data), which also means moving the store frees little until those projects are gone.
entries.regenerates: yes - on the next pnpm install
entries.method: Let pnpm remove packages no project references.
entries.notes: Hard links: bytes are shared with projects' node_modules.

entries.name: Yarn cache
entries.creator: Yarn (Node.js package manager)
entries.purpose: Downloaded package cache.
entries.breaks: Next installs download again.
entries.method: Quarantine, or let Yarn clear it.

entries.name: NuGet packages and caches
entries.creator: NuGet (.NET SDK, Visual Studio)
entries.purpose: Global package folder and HTTP cache.
entries.breaks: Next restore downloads again; open Visual Studio solutions may fail to build until restored.
entries.method: Close Visual Studio / dotnet builds, then quarantine, or let NuGet clear it.

entries.name: Gradle caches
entries.creator: Gradle (Android Studio and Java builds)
entries.purpose: Dependency cache, build cache and downloaded Gradle distributions.
entries.breaks: Next build downloads again; running Gradle daemons may error.
entries.method: Stop Gradle daemons and Android Studio, then quarantine.

entries.name: Cargo registry and git caches
entries.creator: Cargo (Rust)
entries.purpose: Downloaded crate sources and git dependencies.
entries.breaks: Next build downloads again.
entries.method: Quarantine.

entries.name: Conda package cache
entries.creator: Conda (Anaconda / Miniconda)
entries.purpose: Downloaded package archives and extracted packages.
entries.breaks: Environments that hard-link into it keep working; new installs download again.
entries.method: Let conda remove unused packages and tarballs.

entries.name: Go build cache
entries.creator: Go toolchain
entries.purpose: Compiled package cache.
entries.breaks: Next build recompiles.
entries.method: Quarantine, or let Go clear it.

entries.name: Playwright browsers
entries.creator: Playwright (browser automation)
entries.purpose: Chromium / Firefox / WebKit builds used by Playwright scripts.
entries.breaks: Playwright scripts fail until browsers are installed again.
entries.method: Quarantine.
entries.command: reclaim apply --only <id>      (restore later: npx playwright install)

entries.name: Hugging Face cache
entries.creator: Hugging Face libraries (transformers, diffusers, huggingface_hub)
entries.purpose: Downloaded models and datasets.
entries.breaks: Scripts download the models again on next use (often many GB).
entries.method: Quarantine, or pick models to drop in the interactive cache tool.

entries.name: Ollama models
entries.creator: Ollama
entries.purpose: Downloaded model weights.
entries.breaks: Ollama cannot find the models until OLLAMA_MODELS points at the new folder.
entries.method: Quit Ollama, move the folder, then point Ollama at the new location and restart it.
entries.command: setx OLLAMA_MODELS "<new path>"      (after the move; restart Ollama)

entries.name: LM Studio models
entries.creator: LM Studio
entries.purpose: Downloaded model weights.
entries.breaks: LM Studio shows no models until its Models Directory points at the new folder.
entries.method: Quit LM Studio, move the folder, then LM Studio > My Models > change the Models Directory.

entries.name: Claude Code home (.claude)
entries.creator: Claude Code (Anthropic CLI)
entries.purpose: Settings, plugins, session transcripts and memory. May contain credential files.
entries.breaks: Claude Code loses settings, plugins, history and any credentials stored there.
entries.method: Never quarantine. Old session transcripts are pruned by Claude Code's cleanupPeriodDays setting.
entries.notes: May contain credential files; never moved by Reclaim.

entries.name: Claude desktop caches
entries.creator: Claude desktop app (Electron)
entries.purpose: Browser-engine caches of the desktop app.
entries.breaks: The app starts a little slower once. Conversations live in the cloud and stay.
entries.method: Quit Claude desktop, then quarantine.

entries.name: Cursor home (.cursor)
entries.creator: Cursor editor
entries.purpose: Installed extensions and editor settings.
entries.breaks: Extensions and settings are lost.
entries.method: Remove unused extensions from inside Cursor.

entries.name: Cursor caches
entries.creator: Cursor editor (Electron)
entries.purpose: Browser-engine caches, cached builds and downloaded extension packages.
entries.breaks: Cursor starts slower once; nothing else.
entries.method: Quit Cursor, then quarantine.

entries.name: VS Code caches
entries.creator: Visual Studio Code (Electron)
entries.purpose: Browser-engine caches, cached builds and downloaded extension packages.
entries.breaks: VS Code starts slower once; nothing else.
entries.method: Quit VS Code, then quarantine.

entries.name: Grok tooling home (.grok)
entries.creator: Grok command-line tooling (xAI)
entries.purpose: Settings and session data of the Grok CLI. Contents are not catalogued here.
entries.breaks: Grok tooling loses its settings and sessions.
entries.method: Inspect it yourself before touching anything inside.

entries.name: Docker Desktop disk image
entries.creator: Docker Desktop (WSL 2 backend)
entries.purpose: Virtual disk holding every Docker image, container and volume.
entries.breaks: Moving or removing it by hand destroys all images, containers and volumes, and Docker Desktop fails to start.
entries.regenerates: an empty disk is recreated; its contents are not
entries.method: Prune inside Docker, then compact: quit Docker Desktop, wsl --shutdown, diskpart: select vdisk file="<path>" / compact vdisk. Relocate via Docker Desktop > Settings > Resources > Disk image location.
entries.command: docker system prune -a      (removes unused images/containers inside Docker)
entries.notes: The vhdx never shrinks on its own after pruning.

entries.name: WSL distribution disk
entries.creator: WSL 2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux)
entries.purpose: The whole filesystem of a Linux distribution.
entries.breaks: The distribution and everything in it is lost if moved or removed by hand.
entries.method: Move it with WSL itself (list distros: wsl -l -v).

entries.name: Virtual hard disk
entries.creator: A virtualization or backup tool; the file itself does not say which
entries.purpose: A virtual machine's or backup's disk image.
entries.breaks: The VM or backup that uses it breaks if it is moved without that tool knowing.
entries.method: Find the owning tool and move it from there (Hyper-V Manager > Move, VirtualBox Media Manager).

entries.name: Disc image
entries.creator: Downloaded or created by you (installer or OS media)
entries.purpose: Installer or disc image.
entries.breaks: Nothing in Windows; you would re-download it to reinstall from it.
entries.method: Move to Y:.

entries.name: Packet capture
entries.creator: Wireshark / dumpcap / tcpdump
entries.purpose: Recorded network traffic.
entries.breaks: Nothing in Windows; the capture is no longer at this path.
entries.method: Move to Y:.

entries.name: Wireshark temporary captures
entries.creator: Wireshark / dumpcap during live capture
entries.purpose: Unsaved live captures Wireshark writes to Temp while capturing.
entries.breaks: Captures you never saved are gone from Temp.
entries.method: Quit Wireshark, then quarantine.

entries.name: Adobe media cache
entries.creator: Adobe Premiere Pro / After Effects / Media Encoder / Audition
entries.purpose: Conformed audio, peak files and indexes for imported media.
entries.breaks: Projects re-conform media on next open (slow first open).
entries.method: Quit Adobe apps, then quarantine. Alternative: Premiere > Preferences > Media Cache > Delete Unused.

entries.name: Store app data (Packages)
entries.creator: Microsoft Store (UWP/MSIX) apps
entries.purpose: Per-app settings, caches and databases. WSL distributions also live here.
entries.breaks: Apps lose settings and data; WSL distributions are destroyed.
entries.method: Per app: Settings > Apps > (app) > Advanced options > Reset.

entries.name: Installed Store apps (WindowsApps)
entries.creator: Microsoft Store
entries.purpose: Installed Store app binaries.
entries.breaks: Store apps stop working.
entries.method: Uninstall, or move an app to another drive: Settings > Apps > (app) > Move.

entries.name: Downloads folder
entries.creator: Your browsers and you
entries.purpose: Files you downloaded.
entries.breaks: Nothing in Windows; the files are no longer in Downloads.
entries.method: Move to Y:.

entries.name: Desktop folder
entries.creator: You, and installers that drop shortcuts
entries.purpose: Files and shortcuts on the desktop.
entries.breaks: Everything disappears from the desktop until moved back.
entries.method: Move to Y:.

entries.name: Recycle Bin
entries.creator: Windows Explorer (files you deleted)
entries.purpose: Deleted files kept so they can be restored.
entries.breaks: Those deleted files can no longer be restored.
entries.regenerates: fills again as you delete things
entries.method: Empty it yourself. Other users' bins are only visible elevated.
entries.command: Clear-RecycleBin -DriveLetter <D>      (permanently deletes - Reclaim never runs this)
entries.notes: Unelevated you see only your own bin.

entries.name: System Volume Information (restore points, shadow copies)
entries.creator: Volume Shadow Copy Service, System Restore, search indexer
entries.purpose: Restore points, shadow copies (Previous Versions) and volume metadata.
entries.breaks: Restore points and previous versions are lost.
entries.regenerates: yes - new restore points are created
entries.method: See usage with: vssadmin list shadowstorage (elevated). Cap it, or delete old restore points in System Protection.
entries.notes: Only an elevated run can measure it.

entries.name: OneDrive folder
entries.creator: Microsoft OneDrive
entries.purpose: Files synced with OneDrive.
entries.breaks: Moving the folder by hand breaks sync.
entries.method: Right-click files or folders > 'Free up space' to make them cloud-only; they then occupy 0 bytes on disk.
entries.notes: Cloud-only placeholders show their full size but occupy nothing; Reclaim counts them as 0 on disk.

entries.name: OneDrive staging folder
entries.creator: Microsoft OneDrive
entries.purpose: Temporary download/upload staging on a non-system drive.
entries.breaks: Transfers in progress restart.
entries.method: Quit OneDrive, then quarantine.

entries.name: TeamViewer logs
entries.creator: TeamViewer
entries.purpose: Connection and service logs.
entries.breaks: Log history is gone. The current log is locked while TeamViewer runs.
entries.method: Quit TeamViewer and stop its service, then quarantine (Program Files needs an elevated run).

entries.name: PostgreSQL data directory
entries.creator: PostgreSQL server
entries.purpose: Live database files.
entries.breaks: Databases are corrupted or lost if files are moved.
entries.method: Drop unused databases or VACUUM FULL inside psql. Relocate by stopping the service and changing data_directory.
entries.command: psql -U postgres -c "SELECT datname, pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(datname)) FROM pg_database ORDER BY pg_database_size(datname) DESC;"

entries.name: PostgreSQL write-ahead log
entries.creator: PostgreSQL server
entries.purpose: Write-ahead log. Grows without bound when a replication slot or archive_command is stuck.
entries.breaks: Never remove by hand: the database becomes unrecoverable.
entries.method: Find the stuck slot or archiver and fix it in PostgreSQL; WAL is then recycled automatically.
entries.command: psql -U postgres -c "SELECT slot_name, active, restart_lsn FROM pg_replication_slots;"

entries.name: node_modules
entries.creator: npm / pnpm / yarn install
entries.purpose: A project's installed JavaScript dependencies.
entries.breaks: That project won't run or build until you reinstall; the same versions come back only if the project has a lockfile.
entries.method: Stop that project's dev servers, then quarantine.

entries.name: Installed programs
entries.creator: Program installers
entries.purpose: Installed applications.
entries.breaks: Programs stop working.
entries.method: Uninstall programs you don't use.

entries.name: Windows system files
entries.creator: Windows Setup and Windows Update
entries.purpose: The operating system.
entries.breaks: Windows breaks.
entries.method: Only through Disk Cleanup (system files) or DISM.
entries.command: cleanmgr.exe /d C:      (elevated; Clean up system files)

entries.name: Installer package cache
entries.creator: WiX/Burn bootstrappers (Visual Studio, .NET, VC++ redistributables)
entries.purpose: Installers kept for repair, update and uninstall.
entries.breaks: Repair, update and uninstall of those products fail.
entries.method: Uninstall the products instead.

entries.name: Windows Search index
entries.creator: Windows Search service
entries.purpose: Index behind Start menu and Explorer search.
entries.breaks: Search is slow or empty until the index is rebuilt.
entries.method: Indexing Options > Advanced > Rebuild, or trim indexed locations.

entries.name: Delivery Optimization cache
entries.creator: Delivery Optimization service
entries.purpose: Update and Store downloads shared with other PCs.
entries.breaks: Nothing; files download again when needed.
entries.method: Disk Cleanup > 'Delivery Optimization Files', or the cmdlet below.

entries.name: GPU shader caches
entries.creator: DirectX and the GPU driver
entries.purpose: Compiled shaders so games and apps start faster.
entries.breaks: The first launch of games/apps stutters while shaders recompile.
entries.method: Close games and 3D apps, then quarantine.

entries.name: GPU driver installer leftovers
entries.creator: NVIDIA / AMD driver installers
entries.purpose: Extracted or downloaded driver packages kept after installation.
entries.breaks: Nothing; a reinstall downloads the driver again.
entries.regenerates: yes - on the next driver install
entries.method: Quarantine (ProgramData needs an elevated run).

entries.name: Internet cache (WinINet)
entries.creator: Windows internet stack (IE mode, Office, older apps)
entries.purpose: Downloaded web resources for apps that use the Windows internet stack.
entries.breaks: Those apps fetch content again.
entries.method: Close Office and IE-mode pages, then quarantine. Locked files stay.

entries.name: File History backups
entries.creator: Windows File History
entries.purpose: Versioned backups of your libraries.
entries.breaks: Backups and old versions are lost.
entries.method: Control Panel > File History > Advanced settings > Clean up versions.

entries.name: CHKDSK recovered fragments
entries.creator: CHKDSK (disk check after file system corruption)
entries.purpose: File fragments CHKDSK recovered; original names are lost (FILE0000.CHK).
entries.breaks: Nothing in Windows.
entries.method: Move to Y: in case something in it matters.

entries.name: Windows Installer rollback data
entries.creator: Windows Installer (msiexec)
entries.purpose: Rollback files for installs in progress.
entries.breaks: An interrupted install could not roll back.
entries.method: Leave it; Windows Installer cleans it.

entries.name: Temporary user profile
entries.creator: Windows User Profile Service (when a real profile failed to load)
entries.purpose: A throw-away profile Windows used for a session; anything saved during that session is here.
entries.breaks: Files saved during that temporary session are no longer at this path.
entries.method: Move to Y: from an elevated run, then look through it.

entries.name: Puppeteer browsers
entries.creator: Puppeteer (Node.js browser automation)
entries.purpose: Chrome / Chrome for Testing builds downloaded for Puppeteer scripts.
entries.breaks: Puppeteer scripts fail until a browser is downloaded again.
entries.regenerates: yes - npx puppeteer browsers install chrome
entries.method: Quarantine.
entries.command: reclaim apply --only <id>      (restore later: npx puppeteer browsers install chrome)

entries.name: Rust toolchains
entries.creator: rustup (Rust installer)
entries.purpose: Installed Rust compilers and standard libraries, one folder per toolchain.
entries.breaks: cargo and rustc stop working for a removed toolchain.
entries.method: List with 'rustup toolchain list' and uninstall the ones you don't use.

entries.name: Editor global state database
entries.creator: Cursor / VS Code
entries.purpose: SQLite database with the editor's global state: extension and UI state, and in Cursor the chat history.
entries.breaks: The editor loses that state (in Cursor: chat history).
entries.regenerates: an empty database is recreated; its contents are not
entries.method: Shrink it from inside the editor (delete old chats and workspaces). Never touch it while the editor runs.

entries.name: Editor global state database backup
entries.creator: Cursor / VS Code
entries.purpose: Backup copy of state.vscdb the editor keeps to recover from a corrupted state database.
entries.breaks: No recovery copy until the editor writes a new one.
entries.regenerates: yes - written again by the editor
entries.method: Quit the editor, then quarantine.

entries.name: OneDrive sync databases
entries.creator: Microsoft OneDrive
entries.purpose: Sync engine state: which files are synced, where, and in which version.
entries.breaks: OneDrive has to rebuild its state and rescan every synced file.
entries.regenerates: yes - by a full OneDrive resync
entries.method: Leave it. If it is corrupt, a OneDrive reset rebuilds it (onedrive.exe /reset).

entries.name: Microsoft Defender data
entries.creator: Microsoft Defender Antivirus
entries.purpose: Definition updates, scan history, quarantined threats and support logs.
entries.breaks: Antivirus protection and history. The service locks these files.
entries.method: Leave it; Defender manages its own retention.

entries.name: Application-bundled node_modules
entries.creator: An installed program or editor extension that ships its own JavaScript dependencies
entries.purpose: Part of an installed application or extension, not of a project you build.
entries.breaks: The program or extension stops working.
entries.regenerates: no - reinstall the program or extension to restore it
entries.method: Leave it. Uninstall the program or extension if you no longer use it.

entries.name: Global Node.js packages (npm -g, nvm)
entries.creator: npm install -g, the Node.js installer, or nvm
entries.purpose: npm itself and every command-line tool installed globally for this machine's Node.js.
entries.breaks: npm, npx and every globally installed CLI stop working (possibly including the tools running this cleanup).
entries.regenerates: no - each global package has to be installed again
entries.method: List them with 'npm ls -g --depth=0' and uninstall the ones you don't use.
